_comment: COUPLING tier-2. Verifies SPARTA's row in the sides table, which is the one row that says a backend CANNOT take a side: 'not natively' in the Neumann column. Derives the nine surf_collide styles from the SurfCollideStyle(...) registrations in the installed SPARTA source, derives the four that take a thermal datum from which of them call SPARTA's own parse_tsurf (a surface TEMPERATURE parser), and asserts nothing in surf_collide_*.{cpp,h} mentions a flux at all. Then verifies the INDIRECT route the knowledge offers instead — fix_surf_temp.cpp's T = (q/(sigma*emisurf))^(1/4) gray-body conversion and the disclaimer the knowledge quotes verbatim from SPARTA's own doc — because a 'cannot' that hides a workaround steers agents away from a coupling that is possible, which is how this sentence was wrong once already. Finally checks the served payload and the sides table still carry the negative. A negative claim needs a fixture MORE than a positive one: a capability fails loudly the first time somebody uses it, a refusal is never exercised at all.

_mutation.note: Narrow the style-registration pattern so it stops seeing most of the SurfCollideStyle macros: the derived count drops from nine to two and style_list_drifted fires. A count derived from source is only worth anything if it goes wrong when the derivation does, and silently matching fewer files is how such a scan rots. Two by-hand mutations against the subject (neither stageable) each killed this fixture too: appending a line mentioning a prescribed heat flux to the installed surf_collide_diffuse.h, and softening 'There is NO native flux boundary condition' in src/tools/coupling_knowledge.py.
